headline: Post-FOMC relief grind holds NQ near session highs while VIX, yields and crude all ease; Tail stays in the watch band
body: The Federal Reserve raised its target range 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on September 16, its first increase since July 2023, on a unanimous vote, and Chair Kevin Warsh's press conference kept a hawkish tone with projections pointing to a further increase this year. Nasdaq-100 cash sold off to 28,753.29 during that repricing before recovering to close at 28,945.06 (+0.02%), a genuine retracement that argues against a no-retracement regime. Overnight the relief extended: NQ futures trade near 29,582 (+1.1%) with a session range of 29,247.75-29,614.00, leaving price about 30 points below the high. VIX is 15.95 (-9.9%) against a 17.20 prior close, the 10-year yield has eased to 4.97% from above 5.00% and the 2-year to 4.71%, and WTI is near $100.6 (-1.8%) with Brent near $103.2 (-2.5%) as Saudi Arabia works to restore roughly half of the drone-damaged East-West pipeline within days. The persistent overnight direction and the position near the session extreme are the Tail amplifiers; a decaying volatility surface, easing yields, falling crude and yesterday's orderly post-event retracement are the offsets, and cross-assets are not aligned in the pattern that historically denies mean reversion. Stress remains elevated on a newly restarted hiking cycle, a 10-year yield near 5%, crude above $100 and the continuing Strait of Hormuz closure. Shared Finviz cross-asset context was available but stale relative to the freshness threshold, so this assessment rests on independently verified primary sources.

lookbackSummary: Over the past 24 hours the assessment stayed mostly in the low-to-watch Tail band, with one orange excursion to Tail 31% in the 19:00 UTC hour as the FOMC statement and Warsh press conference drove a sharp Nasdaq-100 sell-off toward 28,753. That move retraced into the cash close and Tail fell back to 16-20% overnight. Stress decayed steadily from the high 70s before the decision to the low 60s this morning as volatility normalised, yields eased back below 5% and crude fell on Saudi pipeline repair guidance. The most recent hours have carried a trend-up mode with Tail at 21-22% as the relief grind extended.
outlookSummary: The forecast holds the watch band through the remainder of the European morning, then maps conditional Tail into the block band for the 13:00 and 14:00 UTC hours, covering the 12:30 UTC US data cluster, the 13:30 UTC cash open and 14:00 UTC pending home sales. An aligned bullish regime running into the New York open is the configuration most capable of producing opening continuation with shallow pullbacks, so that window carries the peak conditional Tail of 26%. Conditional Tail then decays through the US afternoon, rises slightly into the 19:00 UTC power hour, and falls below the watch threshold overnight as the event stack clears, before edging back to the watch band during Friday's European morning. Confidence declines with distance from the evidence cutoff. Next-week US calendar items are included where release times were verified.
